subject: The Papyrus · Egypt's first atom
html:
A power station unlike any Egypt has built before

On the Mediterranean coast, about 300 km northwest of Cairo, Egypt is building its first nuclear power plant — and the region's. El Dabaa will house four VVER-1200 reactors for a combined 4,800 megawatts (4.8 GW), enough to be a meaningful slice of national electricity. Construction began in 2022; the first unit is targeted to reach the grid around 2028, all four by roughly 2030. (Source: El Dabaa Nuclear Power Plant.)

Read the financing, not just the ribbon

The headline cost is about $30 billion — but the number that actually matters is who pays. Russia (through Rosatom, which is building it) finances roughly 85% via a 22-year state loan. So El Dabaa isn't only an energy project; it's also a multi-decade debt and a long strategic tie, repaid well into the 2040s. A power plant is a physics story on the surface and a finance story underneath — and the finance story is the one that outlasts the concrete.

We flag the soft edges honestly: the cost is cited around $28.75–30bn depending on source, and the grid and completion dates are projected, not delivered — big infrastructure slips. But the shape is clear: Egypt is joining the small club of nuclear-powered nations, on borrowed money and a long clock.
